title: Mercy and forgiveness
intro: Allah is ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim – and He asks us to be merciful and to forgive one another.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: O My servants who have wronged themselves, do not lose hope in Allah’s mercy! Allah forgives all sins – He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful. <small>(Qur’an, Az-Zumar 39:53)</small>

Allah chose that His names ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) and ar-Rahim (the Most Compassionate) are the first names mentioned in the Qur’an. Every time we say Bismillah we are reminded of them. The message is clear: Allah (SWT) is the Most Merciful and the Most Compassionate. He says that He has written mercy upon Himself. (Qur’an, Al-An‘am 6:12)

learn.label: Every time we begin
learn.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

learn.html: Following his Lord’s guidance, the Prophet (SAW) was merciful and loved to forgive people. Abu Hurayrah (RA) tells that the Companions once asked him to curse the idol-worshippers. He said: “I was not sent to curse, I was sent as a mercy.” (Muslim)

Another time some Companions came and said: “O Messenger of Allah, the tribe of Daws refuse to accept Islam, so pray against them.” People there said: “They are finished!” But the Prophet (SAW) said: “O Allah, guide the Daws and bring them (to Islam).” (Muslim) His dua was answered: a few days later they came and all accepted Islam.

From these ayahs and hadiths it is clear that a believer must be merciful to the people they live with and meet every day. Just as it is impossible to live in this world without mistakes towards others, it is also impossible to live without mercy for each other – mercy brings peace and happiness to the community. Mercy starts with those closest to us: parents, brothers, sisters, relatives, friends and neighbours.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Allah is merciful to those who are merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heaven will be merciful to you.” (Tirmidhi)

Mercy is closely tied to forgiveness. A merciful person usually forgives a hurtful word or a wrong that was done to them. Allah (SWT) is also al-Ghaffar – the One who forgives. He forgives His servants their sins if they repent.

The Prophet (SAW) forgave what others would never have forgiven. He forgave the idol-worshippers their insults and cruelty – they had driven him out of his home town Makkah, did not let him live in peace and spread Islam, and fought against him with their allies. Even so, he forgave them on the day Makkah was freed.

He asked them: “O Quraysh! What do you think I will do with you?” They answered, secretly hoping it was not their end: “Only good. You are a noble brother and the son of a noble brother – and you have power!” Then the Prophet (SAW) said: “I say to you what my brother Yusuf said: ‘No blame on you today. Allah will forgive you – He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.’ Go, you are free!”

In the same way, Allah (SWT) and His Messenger (SAW) ask us Muslims to forgive, if we want to be forgiven too. We should forgive everyone – especially our family, friends, neighbours and fellow believers, and people in general.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Examples of mercy are everywhere around us – even a mother bird caring for her chicks in the nest!

practice.title: The day Makkah was freed
practice.prompt: Put the story in the right order.
items: The Quraysh drive the Prophet (SAW) out of Makkah
They fight against him with their allies
Makkah is freed and the Quraysh wait to hear what he will do
He reminds them of the words of his brother Yusuf (AS)
He tells them: “Go, you are free!”

practice.title: Match the pairs
pairs: the Prophet prayed for their guidance

practice.title: Mercy starts close to home
practice.prompt: Tap everything that shows mercy or forgiveness, then tap Check.

options.text: 🤗 Forgiving your brother who broke your toy
🐦 Putting out water for birds in summer
👵 Helping an old neighbour carry her shopping
😤 Remembering every mistake and paying it back
options.why: The Prophet (SAW) forgave even those who drove him out of Makkah.

options.text: 🙄 Laughing at someone who is sad
options.why: Allah is merciful to those who are merciful to others.

questions.q: Which two names of Allah are the first ones mentioned in the Qur’an?
What did the Prophet (SAW) do when asked to pray against the Daws?
Who should we show mercy to first?
options: Those closest to us: family, friends, neighbours

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) say to the Quraysh when Makkah was freed?
options: “No blame on you today… Go, you are free!”

questions.q: Who will Allah be merciful to?
options: Those who are merciful to others

practice.title: Questions, tasks and talking with your teacher
prompts: 💬 Who should we be merciful to?
🕋 Who did the Prophet (SAW) forgive on the day Makkah was freed, and what did he say to them?
🔗 How are mercy and forgiveness connected?
🤝 Talk with your teacher: when were you last merciful to someone, and when did you last forgive someone? Should every Muslim have more of these moments?
🐾 Task (choose one): find an example of mercy in the animal world and draw a lesson from it for people.
